utterances.text: If we could have a clarification, a point of clarification. On document 4480, I see that it says one of two pages, but at the top it has 7 circled. And if my memory serves me correctly, it would appear that this comes -- this was generated by someone else, perhaps by SpatBat [sic] or someone else, but I don't see how it jibes with number 7 in the circle at the top and at the bottom it says 1 of 2. So perhaps we could have an explanation from the gentleman who obviously would know about this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know about the 7, but this is for sure the document that I typed out and was sent to the Spanish Battalion. It was sent to the Spanish Battalion by way of radio communication or other channels of communication or -- or through international representatives, but this is what had been agreed upon, and it was supposed to be conveyed to the Spanish Battalion. Now, in what way I cannot tell you for sure now. However, on the basis of this that is written here, what happened happened on the 25th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Buljko, you just told us that you think that it was Bruno Stojic who was present at the meeting. Perhaps I could refer you to the top of page 12 of the English version of your statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petkovic, I hadn't seen you. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wished to have this witness clarify a very important question. Why was it sent to the Spanish Battalion in Jablanica? He drafted this document and sent it to Jablanica. What is important is the role of the Spanish Battalion in Jablanica in view of the convoy that was going to Mostar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, is this not a question that's more appropriate for cross-examination rather than in the middle of the Prosecution's direct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I think this is a question that needs to be put during the cross-examination, but as we will not come back to this, why was this document sent to the Spanish Battalion in Jablanica? It could have been sent elsewhere, couldn't it? Could you explain this to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know about that. What was said that this should be sent to the UNPROFOR Spanish Battalion in Jablanica. The negotiating parties, maybe Mr. Albert Benabou, who was an intermediary, and the others, they probably knew why this was being sent to the Spanish Battalion in Jablanica. I don't know. I really don't know. At that time I didn't pay any attention. I had just focused on having the humanitarian aid brought in, and whether it was sent to Jablanica, Medjugorje, Sarajevo or Zagreb, I really wasn't interested in that. What mattered was that they get prepared as a battalion that did have this duty of securing this convoy that was supposed to arrive at the agreed place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In other words, it's Mr. Benabou who told you to write in "Jablanica." You didn't write that, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was taking notes, as I said, and I wrote "Jablanica," as I was told to do. They got the working version that I had typed out. They looked at it, and they gave it to me for amendments, and this is the final version. Had they told me to change Jablanica to Medjugorje, I would have done that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow me, I am a bit confused by what the witness is saying. Can we find out at all who the signatory of this document is, because as the witness put it, it seems that he was told to write this, but as far as I can see, it's the War Presidency of Mostar and the 4th Corps and the commission for exchanges that is submitting this. So that is one negotiating party. This is not a record that was sent on behalf of the international observers. Let's see who the signatory of this document is. That is what is confusing. Was this sent one-sidedly or did someone from the international community ask for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was sent through the commission for exchanges, but this was a confirmed agreement by way of UNPROFOR as stated here about the agreement between the army of the BH and the HVO through UNPROFOR. Mr. Albert Benabou coordinated on behalf of the civilian police of the UN.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In paragraph 7, we can see that the witnesses are Cedric Thornberry, UNPROFOR Colonel Morales from the Spanish Battalion, and from the HCR Mr. Jerry Hume, and Cedric Thornberry, UNPROFOR civil affairs. So the three people mentioned in paragraph 7 are people who were aware of the content of the document.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN BULJKO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. They were fully aware of each and every second of the negotiations taking place on the 24th of August, and it had started even a bit before that. But it is the 24th of August, 1993, that is important, when a final agreement was reached. So you have it stated there explicitly the names and surnames of the representatives of the international community who testified that there was an agreement between the ABiH and the HVO on the 24th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does the witness know that Colonel Morales was the commander of the Spanish Battalion Medjugorje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How can he sign something and send that to Jablanica where he just had a small unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He testified to the agreement here reached between the ABiH and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'm very grateful to my case manager who can perhaps assist in answering Mr. Karnavas's query about the number 7 that was noted as being at the top of this particular document to which we are referring as Exhibit 4480. You might note from the witness's statement at page 13 of the English version of the statement, I am afraid I haven't been able to look up where it is in the B/C/S version but I think it should be somewhere around page 17 or 18, it does say that the copy of the message is indexed under number 7 on the listing of handed over documents, and it appears that when the witness handed these documents over to the Prosecution during the taking of the statement that the documents were numbered and, indeed, the documents are listed at the back of the very same witness statement, the statement from 2000, and the Chamber may note that this particular, as it now is, exhibit, appears at item 7, and it was attached to the statement at one stage in its existence as being number 7 and that is why number 7 then appears at the top of both the English and the B/C/S versions. It was obviously something that the Office of the Prosecutor added in the interests of being able to track the document as it was attached to the statement at the time it was taken and handed over. I hope that clarifies matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It does. I thank Madam Prosecutor for that. But it says here "English translation." Was this document translated by the gentleman? Did he send a B/C/S version or did he send an English version? Because the English translation, it's rather unclear. The other thing perhaps the gentleman could answer why are there -- there's no mention as to who was it on behalf of the HVO who made this agreement. There's nothing as to who attended. He's got the names of foreigners but there's nobody on behalf of the parties who entered into this agreement and why weren't they included?

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Your Honour may recall that I was in the process of asking the witness who attended on behalf of the ABiH and on behalf of the HVO, and I believe the witness gave answers to those questions which I'm still not finished in dealing with. I appreciate that their names are not on this agreement. Perhaps that can be a question that I may also ask the witness if I'm given the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So please finish.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Prior to asking the question as to why the names of HVO and ABiH representatives present at the meeting are not contained on this document, I need to clarify a point that I've been trying to clarify for 15 minutes now. If I can refer the witness back to his answer when I asked who was present as a representative for the HVO. Mr. Buljko, you mentioned that you thought it was Bruno Stojic. If I can refer you to your statement from 2000. At the top of page 12 of your statement you say: "Even though Bruno Stojic was not present during the meeting and the negotiations..." I wonder if you're able to clarify then the discrepancy between those two statements.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN BULJKO
utterances.text: As for humanitarian convoys entering Mostar, two certificates were needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours. Your Honours, now I really have to say that the witness should answer the question if at all possible. My learned friend put a specific question, and the witness is supposed to answer the question rather than provide a description. It says that Mr. Stojic -- in his statement it says that Mr. Stojic was not at the meeting, and today he said that he was. He should really start answering questions, otherwise we'll go on forever in this way and it's not in our interest.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: We will get, obviously not this evening, but we will get some more substance regarding that, but my question, perhaps it's my fault for not explaining it correctly. You said earlier this evening that Mr. Bruno Stojic was present on behalf of the HVO during the negotiations and yet at page 12 of the English version of your statement you say even -- and I'm quoting from your statement now: "Even though Bruno Stojic was not present during the meeting ..." So I'm asking you, was he present at the meeting or was he not present at the meeting, because you appear to have given two different answers to that question as to whether he was present at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN BULJKO
utterances.text: Well, the army and the HVO reached an agreement through their representatives. As for the arrival of the humanitarian convoy --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, we cannot go on like this. You have a clear question, and it calls for an answer, yes or no. Was Mr. Stojic present when this agreement was concluded or was he not? It's not a third thing. It's either yes or no, and you should only give yes or no for an answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stojic had to give his approval for the humanitarian convoy, so he was asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We are not here having a normal conversation under -- under friendly people talking to each other this and that. This is a formal process, proceedings according to rules in which a witness, even if it is unpleasant, sometimes is asked to say yes or no and nothing else, just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay. He was present. Mr. Stojic was present at these negotiations.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he was present at these negotiations for the entrance of the humanitarian -- the entry of the humanitarian convoy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Ms. Gillett.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: Then my follow-up question has to be to you, Mr. Buljko, why do you say at the top of page 12 of your statement: "Even though Bruno Stojic was not present during the meeting and negotiations ..." Why do you say that in your statement if, in fact, he was present at the meeting? Why do you say he was not in your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZLATAN BULJKO
utterances.text: He was present with the international community in negotiations for the entrance of the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do respect the efforts being made by my learned colleague, but if the witness was present and kept notes at this meeting then that's all the Prosecutor is asking him, whether at the meeting which he attended Bruno Stojic was present. All the rest is by the by, and I'm sure we'll get to that in due course. But what is being asked is whether he was at the meeting at which the witness was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have 15 seconds, Mr. Witness. Page 11 in your statement you're explaining that the HVO delegation and the ABiH delegation met at the Mostar airport, and you add that Mr. Benabou had been appointed mediator. So we have a meeting with Mr. Benabou, and at the Mostar airport, we have the two delegations. But it continues on on page 12, and you state: "Even though Bruno Stojic was not present, he approved," which is why we have a question. Was Mr. Stojic present at the airport, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the best of my knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, what, he was there? Yes, he was not there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to what they told me, yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According what you said, but did you see him with your own eyes? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I tried to explain the situation to you a moment ago briefly. The message went off to the Spanish Battalion, and it was compiled on the basis of the agreement between the HVO and BH army at their negotiating -- at their negotiations. This was written in the War Presidency as a follow-up to that, and I wrote it on the basis of what I was told by the negotiating parties. The discussions took place through telecommunication means as well, that is to say with the various devices, the radio station and things like that. That's what they used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Anyway, it's time to adjourn. We'll continue tomorrow, and overnight we will go and see what Mr. Benabou actually said. It is five after 7.00. Mr. Karnavas, you have something to add.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just very briefly. Tomorrow perhaps you can warn the gentleman of the consequences for perjury. I think it's important. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GILLETT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't think there is a basis for that assertion. I think, you know, whatever is happening here is clearly confusion at this state, and I think it's a little bit pre-emptive to jump to the conclusion that there is any malice or bad faith involved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was going to say that exactly. So, please, sir, come back for the hearing tomorrow at 2.15. Until then, please meet with no one, neither from Prosecution or from Defence or from the Bench. And we will now meet at 2.15 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 12th day of June, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.04 p.m.
